hook_text: A blacksmith came home in 1879 with a few cocoa beans. Thirty years later, his country grew more cocoa than anywhere on earth.
clip_script: After 1901, Asante was a British colony. Chiefs answered to British officers, and the Asantehene was in exile. But the Golden Stool stayed hidden and safe. Tetteh Quarshie planted cocoa, and African farmers turned the forests into the biggest cocoa producer in the world. British companies dug gold at Obuasi. Railways carried both to the sea. The farmers did the work, but European firms set the price, so in 1937 the farmers refused to sell. Mission schools and Achimota trained a new generation. Soldiers came home from the war asking for freedom. Kwame Nkrumah said: self-government now. On 6 March 1957, the Gold Coast became Ghana.
visual_style: A whiteboard cocoa pod growing into a chart, a railway line from Kumasi to the coast carrying cocoa and gold, a school building, and a final flag-raising on 6 March 1957.
pacing: Builds from the cocoa story to independence.
